html:
This territory marks the Tuscarora in central New York, among the Haudenosaunee. The Tuscarora are an Iroquoian people whose first home was the coastal plain of North Carolina; see Tuscarora (North Carolina).

In the Tuscarora War of 1711 to 1715 they fought the colonists of North Carolina and their Native allies and lost. Hundreds were sold into slavery. Many survivors moved north to the Haudenosaunee, who spoke related languages. In about 1722 they were accepted as the sixth nation of the confederacy, and the Oneida gave them land near their own.

In the American Revolution most Tuscarora, like the Oneida, sided with the rebels, while other Haudenosaunee nations sided with Britain. Afterwards they settled near Niagara Falls, where the Tuscarora Nation still lives, and some joined the Six Nations in Ontario. See also Iroquois.
